title: Create resilient VCR + deterministic mockserver fixtures for cross-SDK streaming + retry edge cases
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: We need deterministic, replayable VCR fixtures and a lightweight mockserver harness that reproduces subtle streaming+retry failure modes across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Current flaky tests mask bugs in streaming partial-commit semantics, idempotency headers, and KV-cache mismatches that only appear under mid-stream network partitions or duplicate token frames. Goal: define a canonical set of reproducible scenarios, implement VCR capture rules for streaming frames (including control frames), build an embeddable mockserver that can simulate delayed frames, truncated responses, out-of-order chunks, and server-side injected 5xx with retry hints. The harness must be language-agnostic so SDK teams can run deterministic CI tests locally and in CI without flakiness.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A VCR capture format for streaming responses that records chunk boundaries, timings (relative), and metadata (status, headers) is defined and documented.
2) Mockserver supports at least 8 pre-defined scenarios (see test_matrix) and can be driven by a deterministic script file.
3) SDK test suites (Python, TS, Go) include a CI job that replays VCRs and assert stable token-level output and retry-count invariants.
4) Failure modes that previously flaked (duplicate final token, missing end-of-stream, lingering open sockets) are reproducibly triggered and fixed or documented with compensating assertions.
5) PRs implementing the fixtures and mockserver land with green CI for all three SDKs and have at least one cross-review from Runtime and QA engineers.
test_matrix: scenario-01: normal streaming (baseline) - verify chunk order and aggregate tokens
scenario-02: truncated stream mid-chunk - client should surface partial output and not deadlock
scenario-03: delayed control frame (EOS) - client must not double-retry if server later sends success
scenario-04: immediate 500 then ok on retry - exercise retry backoff and idempotency header handling
scenario-05: duplicate final token frames (server replays) - client dedup logic verification
scenario-06: KV-cache-invalidation mismatch - simulate server-side cache reset mid-session
scenario-07: backpressure + slow consumer - ensure streaming API exposes backpressure hooks and retries preserve ordering
scenario-08: network partition with in-flight request - validate cancel semantics and SDK reconnect behavior
mock_server_endpoints: POST /v1/responses/stream - script-driven stream with chunk metadata and timing
GET /v1/responses/fixture/:id - return prerecorded stream for replay
POST /internal/test-control - instruct server to inject latency or drop frames for active fixtures
/ws/stream - websocket variant for TS SDK integration tests
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 A.Rahman: Ticket created after recurring flakiness in CI when running streaming contract tests. Captured sample failure logs from TS and Go jobs.
2026-03-11 M.Liu: Drafted VCR schema that records chunk_id, relative_timestamp_ms, headers, and eof_flag. Prototype serializer in python-vcr/format.py (branch: feature/vcr-stream-schema).
2026-03-11 T.Khan (QA): Ran manual replay of failing trace; reproduced duplicate-final-token case using a curl-based mockserver script.

2026-03-12 M.Liu: Implemented mockserver endpoints in tests/mockserver harness (node). Added control route to inject 100ms-2s delays and to simulate socket truncation. Local smoke tests pass for TS and Python.

2026-03-13 P.Santos (Runtime): Reviewed approach; flagged interaction between SDK retry middleware and streaming buffer that may require an SDK change to expose 'final_chunk_id' in event stream. Added as action item.
2026-03-13 M.Liu: Opened PRs for mockserver and VCR serializer (see github_prs). Running cross-SDK CI with the new fixtures; observed one flaky case left (scenario-06 KV-cache-invalidation).
flakiness_notes: Historical flakiness comes from recording timeouts as wall-clock timestamps and not rebasing them relative to request start; that made replays too brittle. Also several SDKs treated streaming chunks as opaque strings and relied on network framing which varies between runtimes. New format normalizes boundaries and encodes control frames explicitly.
next_steps: Finish KV-cache-invalidation script and add deterministic marker events in the VCR so SDKs can detect cache resets.
Add test assertions for retry-count and idempotency header propagation in all SDK suites.
Coordinate with Runtime team to expose 'final_chunk_id' field in event payloads — decide if this is a breaking change or a backward-compatible opt-in header.
Expand CI matrix to run replays on matrix: node 18, python 3.10, go 1.21, and a minimal alpine environment to catch subtle socket behavior.
notes: Prefer a single canonical VCR format (jsonl frames) rather than multiple vendor-specific formats. Keep the mockserver lightweight (node + small binary) so it can be started in CI containers with <50MB overhead. Include a small CLI to 'record' and 'replay' which mirrors the pattern used in our non-streaming VCR infra.
